summary.text: Elbert (Al) Bartell, an independent write-in candidate, Air Force veteran and self-described public policy analyst and mediator, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. Senate seat in Georgia to Jon Ossoff.
He had appeared on Georgia ballots in earlier cycles and said he was running on public participation in policy-making.

paragraphs.text: Elbert Bartell was born in Hagerstown, Maryland, graduated from Hannah Pamplico High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Saint Leo University in 1984.
He served in the U.S. Air Force from 1973 to 1980, and his Ballotpedia survey says he is a Vietnam-era veteran with expertise in air base ground defense and conflict resolution.
Bartell lists his profession as policy analyst and describes himself as a certified mediator who has worked as an independent public policy leader for two decades.

Ballotpedia lists him as a candidate in the 2020 U.S. Senate special election in Georgia, where he received 0.3% of the vote, and as a withdrawn or disqualified independent in the 2020 regular Senate and 2022 governor's races.
Bartell lost to Jon Ossoff, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
